question: What will be the largest difference in margin among swing seats in the 2026 United States Senate election?

calls.reasoning: Late-Oct 2026 polling averages: NC Cooper +10.7, GA Ossoff +8.2 at the D end. KS +0.2D, IA ~R+0.6, NE ~even, AK D+1-2, ME D+1.4 at the R end. Polling-average spread is ~11-12. Taking the max and min across 10 states with ~4-pt per-state errors widens the expected gap: top ~D+12.5, bottom ~R+5, so ~17-18. Red-state polls have historically underestimated Republicans (NE 2024), which pushes the gap upward. A uniform swing does not change the gap. No human market prices this spread; the only Manifold candidates (Fetterman resignation, Warren reelection) are unrelated.
calls.dossier:
- Election day Nov 3, 2026. Resolves on max minus min of the 10 states' final margins (AK and ME use the final RCV round; Georgia uses the first round if there is a runoff; an Osborn margin counts as D). Event window: results through end of 2026. As of Oct 30 the vote is about 4 days away.
- RCP-style averages (uspresidentialelectionnews, Oct 29, 2026): NC Cooper +10.7, GA Ossoff +8.2, MI El-Sayed +3.2, OH Brown +2.6, TX Talarico +2.2, AK Peltola +1.2, ME Troy Jackson +1.4, KS Hamilton(D) +0.2, IA Hinson(R) +0.6.
- Kansas: PollCheck Oct 28 Hamilton 46.1-Marshall 45.2. InsiderAdvantage Oct 14 Marshall 48-47. FiftyPlusOne Hamilton +1.3.
- Iowa: Marist Oct 8-11 Turek 48-Hinson 45. Emerson Oct 5-6 Hinson 47-45.
- Nebraska: averages from Osborn +0.5 to Ricketts +1.2 (Oct 23-28). Polls range from Osborn +7 (Concord, Oct 18) to Ricketts +3 (NPA). In 2024 Osborn polled close and lost by ~6.7.
- Alaska: FiftyPlusOne Oct 28 Peltola 49.7-47.7. DFP RCV simulation 51-49.
- GA: AJC Oct 21 Ossoff 48-40. NC: Quantus Oct 25 Cooper 51-43.
- Mechanism: a uniform national polling miss does not change the spread. Only state-specific (differential) errors do, typically ~3-5 pts SD per state. Taking the max and min across 10 states inflates the range relative to the polling range.
- Searched but not found: the FiftyPlusOne forecast page (empty fetch) and any market on the margin spread.
calls.reference_class: Gap between the most-D and most-R state among ~10 battleground Senate races, compared with the gap in final polling averages (2018-2024 cycles; results' range typically exceeds the polling range by 3-7 pts)

Poll-implied spread is ~13-15 (NC vs IA). Red-state Senate polls historically understated Republicans by 4-7 pts (IA/KS/AK/TX 2020, NE 2024), and idiosyncratic errors widen max-min, so the most-R state probably ends around R+5 to R+8 and the most-D around D+9 to D+12. calls.reconciliation: No web access on this run. Disputes: Iowa polling level (Run 2's single co/efficient R+3 poll vs averages near even across Runs 1/3; I side with the averages, and it's in the bottom cluster either way); Maine's Democratic nominee (unresolvable from the dossiers, but it doesn't matter since Maine sits inside the range); NC lead +10 vs +14 (used ~D+10.5 averages). All runs agree on the mechanism: a uniform national miss leaves the spread unchanged, differential state errors widen it. Carried forward the ~7-pt dispersion shared by all runs. Final numbers rest on the range-statistic reasoning plus a modest differential red-state miss, which gives an unconditional median ~16.5-17 with 25% above the open upper bound.
